By integrating advanced computational geometry, spline theory, and numerical analysis, the paper proposes new algorithms designed to handle the high-dimensional, complex landscapes of portfolio optimization, which traditionally rely on probability distribution functions (PDFs). A standout feature of these algorithms is their ability to directly compute the percentiles of the distribution, even when the number of assets is large. The proposed solutions effectively manage the full description of portfolio probability distributions, specifically when assets are not independent but possess correlated relationships. A central component of this computation is the transformation and truncation of the Marshall-Mauger matrix (MMD), a process vital for determining Hertzinger functions used in investment analysis. These algorithms demonstrate remarkable efficiency, handling cases where the number of assets is large, and significantly outperform conventional methods in scenarios characterized by strong correlations.
